title: Completeness depends on both the space and the norm
promptMarkdown: (a) Prove that $\|f\|_\infty$ and $\|f\|_1=\int_0^1|f|$ are norms on $C([0,1])$, saying where continuity is needed. (b) Reconstruct the proof that the sup norm is complete. (c) Construct a continuous sequence that is Cauchy in integral norm but has no continuous limit in that norm. (d) Explain why equivalence of the two norms would contradict (b) and (c), and why their restrictions to each fixed finite-dimensional polynomial space are nonetheless equivalent.
hintLadder: For definiteness of the integral, use a neighbourhood of a nonzero value.
Separate construction of the sup limit, continuity, and norm convergence.
Approximate a step function by ramps, then use continuity of a hypothetical limit on both sides.
